personality: 1 iOS-Native Clean (Structure) with 8 Hand-Drawn / Journal (Palette & Warmth)
personality_one_liner: Warm, intimate, and emotionally engaging like a caring family, combining WhatsApp's structural clarity with iMessage's organic softness.

spacing.rule: Generous, breathable rhythm. Avoid cramped elements, leverage safe areas, and give chat bubbles ample margins.

do's: Use subtle glass over the ivory background for the bottom tab bar and sticky chat headers.
Use blur on the Voice Call screen over the warm abstract background.
dont's: Never blur chat bubbles or care tracker cards.
Avoid over-layering glass; keep it restricted to structural navigation.

screens.name: Home
screens.purpose: A warm dashboard combining daily care tracking and quick access to family chats.

states.loading: Gentle fade-in skeleton on care cards.
states.empty: Prompt to 'Say good morning to Mom or Dad'.
states.error: Failed to load messages -> 'Take a deep breath and try again' with a retry button.

screens.layout: Header: Large friendly greeting ('Good morning, Alex') with Profile avatar top-right. Section 1 (Care Tracker): One calm, compact care panel for Food, Water, and Sleep with clear status rows and obvious next actions. Section 2 (Recent Chats): An airy edge-to-edge list of Mom, Dad, and My Fam with distinct avatars, readable snippets, timestamps, and restrained unread indicators.

screens.name: Chats List
screens.purpose: Dedicated inbox for the family conversations.
screens.layout: Standard iOS list layout on ivory background. Large (56x56) avatars for Mom (Coral tint), Dad (Blue tint), Group (Clay tint). Right-aligned subtle timestamps.

screens.name: Chat (Direct & Group)
screens.purpose: The core iMessage-inspired conversation view with clear, color-coded bubbles.

states.empty: Start the conversation with a suggested quick-reply chip.
states.error: Failed to send message -> inline red retry icon.

screens.layout: Warm cream chat area with a personal header containing a clear avatar, name, availability state, and voice-call action. Use original iMessage-inspired bubbles with moderate corner rounding: deep eucalyptus for the user's messages, soft coral-tinted bubbles for Mom, dusty-blue-tinted bubbles for Dad, and warm ochre accents for My Fam context. In group chat, show the sender name or avatar when needed. Keep the composer comfortable and responsive with quick prompts, microphone, and send actions.

screens.name: Voice Call
screens.purpose: A warm, intimate, full-screen audio interface to talk to the AI parents.
screens.layout: Full-bleed abstract watercolor background (Coral for Mom, Blue for Dad) with dark gradient scrim. Top: 'Calling Mom' text. Center: Animated waveform using Reanimated, responding to voice volume. Bottom: Live conversation transcript rolling upwards. Controls at bottom: Large glass or solid pill buttons for Mute, Speaker, and a red End Call button.

screens.name: Profile
screens.layout: Settings list pattern. Top section includes an ivory-tinted card explaining 'Mom and Dad are AI companions here to support you.' Toggle for Haptics, Account settings, Data export.

instructions_to_main_agent: Use the My Fam visual language consistently: warm cream (#FFF9F3) backgrounds, white and warm off-white surfaces, deep eucalyptus charcoal (#24302A) primary text, and muted gray-green (#7C847E) secondary text.
Use soft coral (#E88978) for Mom, dusty blue (#6E94A7) for Dad, warm ochre (#C7944D) for My Fam, and soft green (#6FA47D) for completed care check-ins. Keep the colors subtle and accessible.
Keep the interface friendly and readable with Plus Jakarta Sans. Reserve any warmer display treatment for short greetings or emotional moments, never for dense body copy.

Use iMessage-inspired structure without copying iMessage or WhatsApp branding. Prefer lightly tinted incoming bubbles, deep eucalyptus outgoing bubbles, moderate corner rounding, generous spacing, and clear sender identity.
In the Group chat, visually distinguish Mom and Dad through their avatar, name, and accent color. Label perspectives clearly when both parents respond.
Make care tracking feel human and compact: Food, Water, and Sleep should read as simple status rows with obvious actions, not as a medical dashboard.
Use calm, purposeful interaction polish: responsive press states, gentle typing indicators, and a quiet success moment when a care check-in is completed.
Avoid purple or blue-purple gradients, decorative emoji, excessive shadows, tiny low-contrast labels, generic dashboard mosaics, and uniform bubbly cards.
Keep spacing consistent with a 4px/8px rhythm, maintain comfortable touch targets, and give loading, empty, error, and completed states the same warm visual language.
